purpose: Record placement, execution order, recovery and cleanup before the GPU comparison; numerical sources, data and quality gates remain the committed experiment plan.
placement: Prefer one availability zone; record any capacity fallback and its traffic cost. All training uses private peer addresses.
storage: 250GiB encrypted gp3 per worker; keep model objects and checkpoints on persistent disks. Frozen objects are reused through verified hard links.

recovery.when: After all four candidates and their checkpoints are preserved, before candidate selection or any final evaluation.
recovery.method: Terminate the recorded trainable-tail worker only after verified S3 preservation. Launch one replacement of the same type and runtime, restore only its owned objects/checkpoint from S3, and resume the four logical owners from the committed midpoint in fresh processes.
recovery.pass: The entire terminal checkpoint, including all Adam objects, must equal the uninterrupted terminal checkpoint. No new checkpoint is eligible for selection from this replay.
recovery.accounting: Report the repeated 64 updates, replacement startup and repeated development evaluation separately as recovery overhead. At most four GPUs run simultaneously; five physical instances are used over the full trial if replacement succeeds.

finals: Commit every actual development candidate and the fixed selection before final scoring. Failed development arms cannot open their finals. Score every selected final, including failures.
preservation: Verify complete S3 readback hashes for newly produced tensor objects and evidence before terminating their last retained copies. Original parent objects retain their separately verified source inventory.
cleanup: Retire exactly the recorded study instances and their volumes/security group; verify protected CPU services unchanged. Host timers bound compute duration but do not replace cleanup.
